subject: Orchid Health — exec sponsor checklist, risks & procurement path
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@orchidhealth.com>; Diane Kwan <diane.kwan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Exec sponsor summary + immediate asks

Thanks again for the time today — helpful discussion and appreciate the clarity on the three sponsorship priorities. This note captures the highlights and concrete next steps so the execs at Orchid have a single place to reference.

Short summary (from our view)
- Primary business outcome: reduce triage time and DNAs by 18–25% within Q3 through inferred symptom routing and automated patient messaging.
- Key pain: inconsistent latency and high per-call inference cost on current vendor; need predictable economics for a pilot and a path to scale to 10M API calls/month.
- Risk drivers called out by Rajesh: data residency for PHI-adjacent logs, auditability (retention + immutable logs), and procurement SLA language.

Open asks & owners (next 10 business days)
1) Security evidence pack: we will share a short risk matrix mapping Redwood controls to Orchid's requirements (we will include KMS/HSM notes and SOC2 artifact pointers). Owner: Laura (deliver by 2027-03-03). Attachment: Orchid-Risk-Matrix-v1.xlsx (stub).
2) Pilot scope & success metrics: confirm 6-week pilot with throughput target, latency SLO (p95 < 200ms for 1k concurrent), and quality guardrails (prompt set + evals). Owner: Ben (draft SOW by 2027-03-04). Attachment: SOW-draft-Orchid-v0.1.pdf (stub).
3) Procurement timeline: Rajesh to share PO process and required contract provisions; we will surface any non-standard SLA/indemnity asks by our legal team. Owner: Rajesh / Marissa to coordinate.
4) Executive alignment: Megan to confirm sponsor approvals (CEO + Head of Ops) and whether there are budget constraints for Dedicated capacity commitments. Owner: Megan (confirm by 2027-03-05).

Escalation items we noted
- If data residency cannot be met for retained logs, pilot will need a scoped redaction/KV-cache-only approach.
- If SLA windows require 99.99% for the pilot, we will need to propose reserved capacity (Dedicated) — that impacts pricing.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Laura: send the risk matrix (attached) and short FAQ mapping our positions to typical procurement asks.
- Ben: produce a concise pilot SOW (one page + appendix).
- Megan: share the procurement contact and expected timeline (Rajesh in CC on next message).

Thanks all — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min procurement sync once Rajesh shares the process.

Cheers,
Laura
Laura Bennett

- Budget: we have budget for a pilot but need an estimate for reserved burst capacity; please include a high-level cost delta between hosted vs. a small Dedicated pool.

Thanks, all — quick note on procurement path and items we need from Redwood legal/security to speed review:
- Standard PO + SOW expected. We will run a 3-week review once we have the SOW.
- Required: Data processing addendum (DPA) with clear retention windows and a clause for customer-controlled keying if possible.
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (latest), encryption-in-transit proofs, and a short note on log retention / immutable audit logs.
- For pilot billing: we prefer a fixed pilot fee rather than open usage billing. Can you provide a pilot fixed-fee option?

If you can provide the SOW and DPA drafts by 2027-03-04, we can target signatures by mid-March. I’ll schedule procurement intake for Monday.

-Rajesh
